synoptic.summary: Tuesday's strong cold front has passed: Salt Lake airport turned to flow from 300°–340° with snow and fog Tuesday evening, and pressure is rising fast behind it. A short-lived high moves in for Wednesday — dry and clearing, but the NWS launch forecasts keep flow from 110°–150° at 8–12 kt gusting 14–18 kt all day, with no afternoon switch to 320°–360°. That breaks the usual diurnal pattern, and it puts POM North and Cherry in the lee and POM South on the rotor side of its 160° cut-off. A colder storm follows Thursday into Friday: precipitation chances at the launches climb from 35% Thursday morning to 71% by midday and 91–98% Thursday evening through Friday afternoon, with snow levels near or below 5,000 ft by Friday (launch height). Thunder chances are low but non-zero (up to 10% Friday). The winds-aloft download failed this run, so rotor and mixing-down checks rely on the NWS transport wind and the airport forecasts.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Dry conditions are then expected to prevail for most of Wednesday, with southerly winds increasing. The break in the action will be short lived, however, with a somewhat colder system anticipated to move across the area Thursday into Friday bringing the potential for significant snow to the mountains once again, particularly in the Upper Cottonwoods and areas near Brian Head, with light valley snow accumulations looking increasingly likely as well.

pressure.significance: Sea-level pressure at Salt Lake airport (KSLC) rose from 1004.4 mb at 10:54 Tuesday to 1011.0 mb at 18:54 Tuesday (altimeter still climbing, 1012.6 mb at 19:13) — the post-frontal rise ahead of Wednesday's brief high. Expect it to fall again ahead of the Thursday–Friday storm.

observations.summary: Tuesday-evening observations (18:35–19:16 local), all under 3 h old at fetch time, taken right behind the cold front. Readings are mixed and gusty: Salt Lake airport 320°/14 kt with light snow, South Valley Regional 320°/19 kt G34 in snow and fog, Alpine 14°/12 kt G20, Lehi 18°/10 kt G17, while Provo (240°/19 kt, gusts 24–29 kt, rain) and Spanish Fork (210°/12 kt G16, gusts to 21 kt) still show pre-frontal flow. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no data. These are frontal-passage readings 12 h before the Wednesday morning slot — they say little about sunrise; the airport forecasts expect the flow to return to 140°–160° overnight.
